newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown declines to name date for mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown declines to name date for mini-budget.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown declined to confirm that his mini-budget would be presented on June 10.
Asked in a BBC television interview if June 10 was the date, he replied: "I'm not going to give a date until we are ready to announce it."
The new Labour government said it would present a mini-budget within two months of the May 1 election and press speculation has centred on June 10 as the likely date.
Brown said it was important to get moving on the budget.
"What is important to this budget is the reform of the welfare state. We've said we need a new welfare state for the modern era," he added.
Brown again declined to specify which privatised utility firms would pay the windfall tax which is expected to be the centrepiece of the mini budget.
"I said we will announce the category of firms affected in the budget. It will become clear then."
